cases.purpose: ipcctl --rm shm: denied unless BASHOS_IPCRM_ALLOW_RMID is exactly "1" (unset, 0, yes, "1 ", empty, 01), both fixture objects kept; id grammar (word, empty, negative, > INT_MAX, suffix, plus sign) rejected as invalid before the policy check; with the policy only the selected of two util-linux-created objects is removed, with shmctl arguments equal to a libc IPC_RMID call (setup requires exactly shmctl(0,0)); repeated and unknown ids give the IPC_RMID EINVAL diagnostic; usage forms print the usage line; every step has exact status, empty stdout and exact stderr
cases.comparison: Contract: per step, exact status, empty stdout and exact stderr (no shell prefix: ipcctl writes its own diagnostics), and object membership in /proc/sysvipc/shm; ids come from util-linux ipcmk output, never from the candidate. The removal runs under a seccomp user-notification rule that records shmctl (every argument after the id: cmd, buf) and continues it to the kernel; the record must equal the one setup takes from a libc IPC_RMID call under the same rule in an identical namespace, which setup requires to be exactly shmctl(0,0) (cmd IPC_RMID = 0, NULL buffer). Every step runs and the case fails at the end with the mismatch count; raw per-step status/stdout/stderr are appended to observations.txt. Each side runs in a fresh IPC namespace (unshare --user --map-user=2000 --map-group=2000 --ipc): ids are allocated from an empty namespace identically on both sides, POSIX message queues live in that namespace's internal mqueue mount, POSIX shm/sem in the per-side /dev/shm, and everything is destroyed with the namespace. Setup proves the namespace is empty and that util-linux ipcmk/ipcrm work in it.
